Barnaby was a big, floppy dog. His job was to watch the back yard.
Every morning at eight o’clock, Arthur opened the door. Barnaby ran out onto the green grass. He sniffed the air.
Then he saw Pip.
Pip was a grey squirrel. Pip lived in the tall oak tree. Pip was not scared of Barnaby.
"Woof!" barked Barnaby. "Get off my lawn!"
Pip sat on a branch. He held a brown nut. "I am not on your lawn," Pip said. "I am in my tree!"
Pip dropped the nut. Thud! It hit the ground near Barnaby’s paws.
Barnaby did not bite the nut. He picked it up with his mouth. He set it by the tree.
"Here is your nut," Barnaby said. "Now I must do my job."
Barnaby walked around the yard. He checked under the shed. He checked the big red hose. He pushed three brown leaves into a pile with his nose.
Pip ran down the fence. "Why do you push the leaves?" Pip asked.
"To keep the yard clean," said Barnaby.
Pip grabbed a dry yellow leaf. He threw it up in the air. He landed on the grass with a bounce.
"Throwing leaves is fun!" Pip squeaked.
Barnaby looked at a yellow leaf on the ground. He blew air out of his nose. Puff!
The leaf flew into the air. It landed right on Barnaby's black nose.
Pip laughed. "Look at you! You can play!"
Barnaby looked at the leaf on his nose. His tail began to wag.
From the house, Arthur called out, "Barnaby! Come eat!"
Barnaby shook the leaf off his nose. He looked up at the squirrel.
"See you tomorrow, Pip," Barnaby said.
"See you tomorrow, Barnaby!" Pip called back.
